hints: Look closely at the structures of the two acids, methanoic acid has an H attached directly to the C=O group while ethanoic acid does not.
Remember that both acids will show normal acidic behaviour, so they will both fizz with carbonate to give carbon dioxide.
Think about which of the listed reagents are oxidising agents that can tell an easily oxidised acid apart from one that resists further oxidation.
walkthrough:
**Compare the two acid structures**

Both are carboxylic acids, so both show acidic properties. But methanoic acid is special.

$$\text{HCO}_2\text{H} = \text{H-COOH} \quad \text{vs} \quad \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} = \text{CH}_3\text{-COOH}$$

**Spot why methanoic acid can be oxidised**

The H-C=O part of methanoic acid behaves a little like an aldehyde. It can be oxidised further to $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$$\text{HCOOH} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test reagent 1 with both acids**

$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3(aq)$ is just an acid-base test. Both acids release $\text{CO}_2$ effervescence.

$$2\text{RCOOH} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{RCOONa} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test reagents 2 and 3 with both acids**

Fehling's reagent and acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ are oxidising agents that oxidise aldehydes. They will oxidise $\text{HCOOH}$ but not $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.

Fehling's: blue to brick-red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate. $\text{KMnO}_4$: purple to colourless.

**Conclude which react differently**

Reagent 1 reacts the same with both. Reagents 2 and 3 react differently, oxidising methanoic acid only. That gives statements 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This combination includes statement 1. Sodium carbonate reacts the same way with both acids, giving effervescence of CO2, so it cannot distinguish them.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination includes statement 1 but omits statement 3. Statement 1 is wrong because both acids neutralise carbonate, while statement 3 is correct and should be included.
options.C: Correct. Fehling's reagent and acidified KMnO4 both oxidise methanoic acid to CO2 and water on heating but have no effect on ethanoic acid, so they react differently. Sodium carbonate reacts identically with both.
options.D: Incorrect. This combination claims only statement 1 distinguishes the acids. In fact statement 1 shows no difference, while statements 2 and 3 do show a difference.
